Dear User, You are currently using the wrong username ()to collect data. Please note that to ensure data security, all data collection is expected to be done with the username: enumerator. Please contact your field supervisor for the further details.

Baseline, 2017
Household Survey
Instructions The main respondent of this survey should be the most knowlegeable household member, preferably in this order: - Household Head - Primary Care Giver of Selected Child - Spouse of Household Head - Any other knowledgeable Adult household member (18 years or Older)

Good day, my name is . I work with Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA). IPA is a research organization with its head office in the US. IPA is working with researchers to learn more about young children and about how we can improve children's learning outcomes. We have received official permission from the Ghana Education Service to conduct this survey.
Procedures
As part of this study, we are conducting a household survey which asks some information about your household, such as its demographics, your educational history as well as that of other household members, dwelling, land, livestock, assets, engagement in economic activities, income and consumption expenditures and prices available in your community. Afterward, a caregiver of a selected child in this household will be interviewed separately for some information about the caregivers' background, child care practice and beliefs, social networks and physical and psycho-social well-being, as well as some information about the development of the children in this community. I will be also spending some time with the selected child from this household to take him/her through some games. I would like to invite you to participate in this survey. Both interviews plus the games with the child combined will last about 3 hours. After this round of the survey, we will revisit, first, your child at his/her school to take the child through some games at the school. Then, lastly, we will revisit this household here in the future to ask you more questions. We will in the next follow up round take your child through games at their school. Please note that even if you agree now to take part in such future survey, you may change your mind later and notify us of such change when we come back. That is, your consent will be sought any time we come to conduct a follow-up survey.
Confidentiality
Kindly note that all your responses and that of your child will be anonymized and will be held in confidence. Only the researchers involved in this study and those responsible for research oversight will have access to the information you provide which identifies you or your child. You and your child's responses will be numbered and the code linking the number with your names will be in an encrypted data file. Researchers will keep your information confidential to the extent possible and allowable by the law.
Voluntary Participation
Your participation in this study is voluntary. If at any time, you do not want to answer a question or feel like discontinuing the survey, you are free to do so. Your decision will not result in any penalty. Also, refusing to participate would not affect you or your communities' eligibility to receive any program or funds or services. Also, even if you agree to participate in the study now, no one from IPA will be allowed to ask you or your children additional questions in the future without asking for your consent again.
Risks and Benefits
There is no risk for you if you decide to participate in the study. There are no benefits either. You are responses to this study will help to shape education policies in Ghana. You will be offered cakes of soap as a thank you for participating in this study.
Contact Information
You can ask any questions that you have about the study now. If you have a question later that you didn't think of now, you can contact IPA at +233 030-279-0372 and ask the Research Associate, or the Research Manager, with any questions or concerns.
Agreement to Participate
I certify that the survey has been explained to me, and I have had the opportunity to ask questions. All questions have been answered satisfactorily. I consent voluntarily to participate as a subject in this study and understand that I have the right to withdraw from the study at any time without in any way it affecting me in any way. I consent to the processing of my personal information for the purposes of this research study. Do you have any questions that I can answer?

select1.label: (C01) Have your questions, if you had any, been answered to your satisfaction?

(C02) Do you understand the procedures I have just described to you? : If the respondent reports not to have understood the procedures, then re-explain the procedures to him/her by re-reading the consent form slowly. Repeat the consent form up to three times if necessary. If after three times the respondent still reports not to have understood the procedures, ask your supervisor for assistance in explaining the procedures to the respondent. If after that effort the respondent fails to understand the procedures, thank the respondent for his/her time and terminate the interview here.
(C03) Do you agree to a written consent to participate in this survey?

During this interview you may be audio recorded. You and the enumerator will both not know when this recording may happen. The audio recording may only happen if you consent to it and you will not be recorded against your will. This recording will only be used for data quality assurance purposes only. Do you consent to a possible audio recording?

(AC00) Before, we start, I will like to inform you about the definition of a household.
What is a household?
A household is a person or a group of persons who:
  • live together under the same roof or compound recognising one person as the head; AND
  • eat from the same pot; AND
  • have lived in the household for at least 30 days consecutively/60 days non consecutively in the last twelve months
Exceptions;
  1. Persons like spouses, babies or other persons who have come to live with the household and NOT JUST VISITING;
  2. Boarding students in the household who spend some time away at school but come home during breaks;
  3. Members who live in accommodation provided by another household because there not enough space in the shelter provide by the household they belong to,
  4. Household head who heads more than 1 household is a member of all households.
Examples of households
: A young man who is unmarried; lives alone in his room or compound and has his own housekeeping arrangement. Will be considered a one member household. If this same unmarried young man is living in the same compound or room with a younger sister or brother and his mother who share the same housekeeping arrangement. This will constitute household of three persons. In another instance, there could be one man who has a wife and six children and out of these six children, only four of them are being accommodated in the same compound whilst the other two children eat from the same pot with the household but because of lack of sleeping space in that compound, an arrangement is made for them to be sleeping with a neighbour. This is still a household of eight persons. , Please ensure that the respondent understands the definition of a household before you proceed. Repeat the explanation if they don't.
